coverage_questions: The paper does not specify the internal preprocessing, hidden-state extraction, or pooling implementation for each BioFM beyond stating that outputs are pooled to a single embedding in the evaluated encoders.
The exact prompt serialization, [BIO] marker position handling, teacher-forcing labels, attention masks, and generation-time decoding inputs are unspecified.
The paper states that BIOVERSE can combine modalities in one LLM, but gives no concrete simultaneous multi-modal input path or receiving-port implementation.
The general-domain LLM used directly as a biological encoder is mentioned conceptually, but its concrete BIOVERSE input trajectory is not documented.

operation_proposals.why_no_existing_operation: The paper documents a modality-specific pretrained BioFM mapping biological inputs to pooled or sequence embeddings, but the catalog has no generic opaque encoder-forward operation. The internal computation and extraction point are not established, so the step remains an unexpanded boundary.

The catalog has correspondence alignment but no operation representing the stated bidirectional cosine-similarity InfoNCE objective with learnable temperature and in-batch negatives. The objective remains an unexpanded training boundary.

evidence.quote: To achieve this, we introduce a CLIP-style alignment stage using paired data ( x b , t b ) , where the projection P θ is trained so that the bio embedding z b = f b ( x b ) is close to its language counterpart ϕ ( t b ) , which represents the text's embedding.
In the base training mode illustrated in Figure 1, all data is processed through LLM's forward pass, and a standard autoregressive cross-entropy loss (with teacher forcing) is used to guide learning.

Biological Encoder We evaluate representative foundation models across three modalities (all pooled into a single embedding at the end): scGPT (Cui et al., 2024) for scRNA-seq, ESM-2 (Lin et al., 2023) for proteins, and ChemBERTa (Chithrananda et al., 2020) for small molecules.

scRNA-seq: For single-cell data, we adopt CellWhisperer (Schaefer et al., 2024), which aligns scRNA-seq profiles with cell-type and tissue-level textual metadata. Following the dataset protocol, we use the CellxGene subset (Perkel, 2024), where pseudo-bulk RNA samples are generated by averaging single-cell profiles, and natural-language descriptions are produced from cell and tissue metadata using large language models.
